The stated healthy HTTP error-rate panel is genuinely green: payment-service error_rate (unit '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)') stayed flat at 0.18-0.26% avg (max 0.32) across every 5-min bucket from 12:17Z to 13:57Z, matching the report's 'error_rate normal'.

A non-HTTP metric shows the true failure: bank_api_error_rate for payment-service is pinned at 100.0% for the entire window (12:17Z-13:57Z, mean 100.0), and payment_success_rate is only ~2.5% (mean 2.48, range 1.44-3.5) — i.e. ~97.5% of bank transfers are failing.

bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no telemetry of its own; it can only be observed through payment-service, its sole caller.

Failed transfers are moved to PENDING_RETRY rather than returning 5xx, which is why the HTTP status-code dashboard (error_rate) stayed green; retries are therefore accumulating without surfacing on that panel.

events.answer: payment-service is NOT healthy: it is failing essentially all bank transfers on its outbound mTLS leg to bank-partner-api (bank_api_error_rate = 100%, payment_success_rate ~2.5%) from at least 12:17Z, while its HTTP 5xx error_rate metric stays green at ~0.21% because failed payments are marked PENDING_RETRY instead of returning 5xx. tasks.objective: Establish the true symptom onset and blast radius for the 12:17-13:59Z window: query logs and metrics for payment-service and its immediate callers/dependencies to verify whether payment-service is actually healthy. Specifically check error_rate, request volume/throughput, latency (p50/p95/p99), timeouts, retry counts, and downstream call failures/outbound errors - not just HTTP status codes. Report if failures appear as timeouts, latency spikes, retries, or async/queue errors that HTTP status dashboards would miss, and identify which service(s) show anomalies first.
tasks.answer: payment-service is NOT healthy: it is failing essentially all bank transfers on its outbound mTLS leg to bank-partner-api (bank_api_error_rate = 100%, payment_success_rate ~2.5%) from at least 12:17Z, while its HTTP 5xx error_rate metric stays green at ~0.21% because failed payments are marked PENDING_RETRY instead of returning 5xx. The cause visible in logs is an expired client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) rejected by bank-partner-api. Onset appears to be ~12:15-12:18Z, just before the reported 12:32Z.

tasks.objective: Across ALL services (not just payment-service), enumerate deploys, config/feature-flag changes, and known historical precedents in the window covering roughly 11:00-13:59Z. Also map payment-service's dependency graph (upstream callers, downstream dependencies such as ledger/bank-integration/gateway, shared databases/queues/PSP connectors) and flag any shared components that other services also depend on. Note any change timing that could precede the 12:17Z symptom onset.
tasks.answer: Across ALL services in 11:00–13:59Z there were zero deployments and exactly one config change: payment-service raised bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000ms at 11:20:00Z (cfg-2502, author p.nair) — i.e. ~57 minutes before the 12:17Z symptom onset. payment-service's dependency graph is api-gateway (caller) → payment-service → {ledger-db (postgres, SHARED), bank-partner-api (external), kafka (SHARED, produce)}. Shared components that other services also use: ledger-db (order-service, portfolio-service, settlement-service) and kafka (order-service, settlement-service, notification-service). Historical precedents include a bank-partner-side payment failure outage (HIST-105) and a ledger-db resource-exhaustion incident (HIST-114).

tasks.objective: Correlate the change list and dependency map from task b against the precise symptom onset and anomalous services found in task a. Determine which single change (deploy or config) best matches the onset time and affected dependency path, and whether the fault lies in payment-service, a downstream dependency, or a shared component - including evaluating the possibility that no internal change is responsible (external bank/PSP issue).
tasks.answer: No deploy (count 0) and only one config change — payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20Z (cfg-2502) — occurred in 11:00–13:59Z; that change precedes the 12:17Z onset by ~57 min and only adjusts a timeout, so it does not match the onset or failure mode. The fault lies on payment-service's outbound dependency leg to bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry), where an expired CLIENT certificate (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15Z) causes the mTLS rejection: this is a payment-service-side credential expiry, not a bank/PSP-side outage and not a shared ledger-db/kafka failure, and no internal change is responsible. Precedent HIST-106 ('Settlement mTLS certificate expired', credential_expiry) is the closest historical match.

tasks.objective: Scope test for H3 vs H1 over 12:00-13:59Z: compare payment-service's bank_api_error_rate / payment_success_rate failure signal against the analogous health of the OTHER shared ledger-db and kafka consumers — order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service. For each, report request success/error rate, latency p50/p95, and any timeouts, queue depths or async errors on their ledger-db and kafka paths, with timestamps of any anomaly. If they are clean/unchanged while only payment-service degrades, H3 (shared component failure) is contradicted; if multiple services degrade together and earlier/at the same time, H3 is supported. As a secondary signal, report payment-service's retry-queue depth / PENDING_RETRY backlog count over the window to confirm the masking mechanism's magnitude.
tasks.answer: H3 (shared ledger-db or kafka component failure) is contradicted by the scope test: across 12:00-13:59Z the three neighbours that share ledger-db and kafka — order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service — are all clean and unchanged (error_rate ~0.2%, flat p99 latency of ~150/179ms, flat db_pool_in_use ~14 conns, and settlement kafka consumer_lag normal at mean 43.4 messages), with no onset or timeouts on their shared paths, while only payment-service degrades (bank_api_error_rate 100%, payment_success_rate ~2.5% per F9). The degradation is isolated to payment-service's single outbound leg, so a shared-component failure is not supported. Secondary signal: payment-service has no retry_queue_depth metric at all, so the PENDING_RETRY backlog can only be evidenced by the 135 log events (first_seen 12:17:57Z, F7), which matches the masking mechanism (failures diverted to retries rather than surfacing as HTTP 5xx).

critiques.summary: H1 is well grounded: the causal chain rests on VERIFIED findings (F7 log naming our own CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal and our own notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; F8/F9/F12 confirming the PENDING_RETRY masking; F13/F14 ruling out deploy/config triggers; F15/F16 placing the failing leg on the external mTLS path). Temporal order is tight (notAfter 12:15Z → first error 12:17:57Z), scope is confined to the outbound external leg, and all recent changes across all services were enumerated. Remaining gaps are confirmation-class: H3's scope test (a shared ledger-db/kafka failure should also hit order/portfolio/settlement) and the exact current cert notAfter/rotation status. I am not fully accepting only because H3's chain has an un-evidenced hop and H1 rests partly on the inferred step 'our cert genuinely expired vs partner-side trust change' — but both of those leave the remediation on our side, so they do not name a different origin. Verdict: needs_evidence for two cheap, obtainable confirmations; cap confidence at 0.85.

challenges.issue: The hop from 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45) + our notAfter' to 'genuine our-side expiry' is an inference, not verified: a partner-side trust-store/rotation change could in principle reject our cert. Unresolved and untestable on the partner side (has_telemetry=false).
Exact onset between 12:15:00Z (notAfter) and 12:17:57Z (first ERROR) is bounded but not pinned; no data before 12:17Z was queried because the task window started there.

H3's causal chain contains an un-evidenced hop ('payment legs fail as a downstream effect') and its scope test is unanswered: if ledger-db/kafka were degraded, order/portfolio/settlement should also show anomalies, but no metric queries were run on them.
Partner-side attribution cannot be positively excluded because bank-partner-api has no telemetry; refuted only indirectly by the alert text naming OUR CN and OUR notAfter.

evidence_requests.rationale: Closes the open questions on exact notAfter and whether the timeout change altered retry behavior; distinguishes the genuine-expiry mechanism from a partner trust change and lets H1 move above 0.85.

evidence_requests.question: Compare payment-service's bank_api_error_rate / payment_success_rate anomaly against the same or analogous failure signals for order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service (the other consumers of shared ledger-db and kafka) over 12:00-13:59Z — do any of them show degradation and when?
evidence_requests.rationale: Direct scope test for H3: a shared ledger-db/kafka degradation should hit multiple services, whereas an isolated payment-service outbound mTLS expiry should not. If they are clean, H3 is definitively contradicted.

critiques.summary: H1 is adequately proven and now survives every test I asked for in round 1. Grounding: every hop rests on VERIFIED findings. The failing hop is a log line quoting OUR OWN client identity and OUR OWN expiry boundary (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, alert 45, 170x) plus 135x 'payment marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (F7). Temporal order is tight and mechanistically consistent: cert notAfter 12:15:00Z → first handshake rejection 12:17:57Z; the proposed cause precedes onset by ~3 minutes, not 57. Scope: the round-1 gap is now closed — the three neighbours sharing ledger-db and kafka (order-service, portfolio-service, settlement-service) are all flat across 12:00-13:59Z (error_rate ~0.2%, p99 ~150/179ms, db_pool_in_use ~14 conns, settlement kafka consumer_lag mean 43.4 no backlog), so the clean-vs-degraded split contradicts H3 (F19-F22). Masking mechanism is verified twice over: HTTP error_rate flat 0.18-0.26% (F8) while bank_api_error_rate=100% and payment_success_rate~2.5% (F9), with latency/throughput unchanged (F10). Alternatives were actually tested, not dismissed: cfg-2502 was enumerated, timed (~57min before onset), and mechanically excluded (timeout only, no latency step) (F2/F14); shared-component failure was killed by the scope test; deploy/rollback eliminated by an all-services count of 0 (F1/F13). H2 is the only rival naming a different origin, and it is not supported: it is contradicted by F7 (the rejection names our cert and our notAfter) and by F18, and it is unfalsifiable from our side only because bank-partner-api is has_telemetry=false (F6/F11) — an unavailable data source, which is a reason for an assumption plus a confidence ceiling, not for another query round. Two residual points I flag below are confirmation-class, not origin-class: the exact sub-two-minute onset instant and whether the peer's alert 45 reflects a genuine past-notAfter rather than a partner-side trust change. Since either reading of the second point still fixes the remediation on our certificate, neither names a competing origin nor a different fix. Verdict: accept.

challenges.issue: The 'genuine expiry vs partner-side trust-store change' ambiguity in H1's own assumptions is unresolvable from our telemetry because bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false (F6/F11); the message text is our only witness. This caps confidence just under certainty — but it does not name a different origin, since both readings put remediation on our client certificate. Record as an explicit assumption rather than a reason to keep querying.

Exact onset is bounded, not pinned: failure is already at 100% in the first 12:17Z bucket and nothing before 12:17Z was queried, so the interval 12:15:00Z-12:17:57Z is inference from the cert boundary plus log first_seen, not a measured first-failure instant. Tight enough that it cannot reorder the ranking.

Not positively refuted from partner-side evidence — it is contradicted only indirectly (F7 names our cert and our notAfter; F18 infers a payment-service-side credential fault). Because the decisive data source is permanently unavailable, this is a live-but-unsupported alternative that the evidence weight (0.12) correctly reflects; it should not be listed as 'contradicted=[]' anywhere it would imply equal footing.

What left the certificate unrenewed (no cert-rotation event in the deploy/config lists) remains unidentified, so the latent trigger behind the expiry is unproven. Root cause of the incident (expired client cert rejected at mTLS) is established; the renewal-process failure is a follow-up, not an obstacle to acting now.
